The gacha system in the game is pretty rough. Even with the pity system there is no guarantee of receiving the skin you want. If you pull 80 times for a resplendent or higher skin, you could just receive another copy of a resplendent or higher skin you already own from the current pool. The good news is that the copy is converted into tokens that can be exchanged for the skin you want. The bad news is that a resplendent skin only gives 200 tokens and the banner skin costs 8,888 tokens. As you can probably guess this can get absurdly expensive. The pity system needs to just award the banner skin at 80 pulls. Additionally the game has connectivity issues that can affect combat pretty heavily. For a free-to-play roguelike shooter, it's pretty decent.
The monetization is mainly for cosmetics though you still can get stuff for free after playing a decent amount to unlock the later modes and completing missions for currency.

The main issues are with the gameplay however :

[h3]Lengthening progression by requiring you clear multiple floors of 'Corrective Action'[/h3]

The game is ok for the first 7 difficulties : You unlock the next difficulty by completing the previous difficulty. However the last 3 each require clearing 10 levels of 'Corrective Action'. It gets tiring real quick because you're playing the same mode with slight variations and increasing debuffs just to unlock the next higher difficulty which gives higher tiers of passive upgrades and/or more stuff you can use to modify your build. This would be fine to a degree, in terms of making the player gain more experience and skill to give them a more challenging experience, if it weren't for the second issue.

[h3]Gameplay is rather stale at the moment due to balancing.[/h3]

Search the top ranks of solo players and you'll see almost everyone going with Arbiter of Music + Skill Build. Why? Because the perks of music do more damage than your character's abilities and are easier to build/scale with. The level design of 'Corrective Action' maps almost feels counter-intuitive to the nature of a roguelike by giving you such a limited number of chances for RNG that you must optimize to defeat the boss at the end.

It is really difficult to make a choice on my vote here. So I will start with the good.

The game is fun. You go in, enter some rogue-lite game with guns, explosions and madness everywhere, and it just keeps on getting more chaotic. Big numbers go brr.
While characters have a different approach, it doesn't really seem to matter half of the time, as most of your damage may come from earned passives through a run, proc'd on using abilities, no matter the character. I guess it just determines if you're more of an AoE person, a single target one, or a little team buffer.

And yet, it's fun enough.

... Until we get to the bad.

This game runs very well, don't get me wrong. But when you have some last-year, top of the market GPU and CPU, and your game faces intense stutter every 10-30 seconds or so, while everything keeps on running so you end up unable to dodge, or you end up killed because you were forcefully stuck on the spot... Or even when you mysteriously lose control over your character saved for WASD and mouselook, it is extremely [b]infuriating[/b].

No leak in processes. No spike on monitors. The game simply decides that it will stutter sometimes. I am unsure why. But until this is fixed, it is very difficult to appreciate the game fully. That issue also isn't just on my end: look it up online, and you will notice that many players experience the same problem.

So my vote will be negative, as long as this issue negatively affects my entire experience.

First off the game is crazy fun. I like to grind and get better gears etc. The replayability is good. There are a few things I THINK (key words here) this game needs immediately for it to shine even brighter: (Note: I will leave out the obvious things such as stuttering fix, matchmaking issues, lag.. its clear that these things need FIXING ASAP but here are other things that probably people have not thought of kana.)

1. Melee - Adds rushing you and can not get them off of you, melee.
2. UI adjustments - the numbers near the reticle prevent me getting perfect reload... annoying.
3. A better map on the loading screen instead of the shapes at the bottom. (kinda like the complete map but have hidden areas left blank if it is possible to explore them)

I will probably update later but for now, the game is so good imo that i continue to play through the stutters and lag. Let the bullets fly! I still recommend this game and I hope that it will be fixed as I am ready to continue leveling up.

Good bones, but so many issues.

Over 50 difficulties across at least 3 areas/modes, each have their own individual matchmaking queues.  Good luck finding a party for anything ever.

The gacha, while currently cosmetic only, has unbelievably terrible rates.  And the only outfit I'd want doesn't even have a pity.  And the pity for the "main prize" is abhorrently expensive.

The character upgrade system is a mess.  Feels like a terrible Tetris rip off where you're fitting weird shapes into a weirder box.

The game could end up really good if the devs make some big sweeping changes, but in it's current state it's not worth it.

A very simple, empty and addicting game play "loop". A very small selection of bosses / characters and even smaller selection of maps - but kind of fun to grind out progression on the possibly 2 or 3 that appeal.

This would be probably enough - if it wasn't for the constant and frustratingly awfully timed stuttering.

In group play you can be stuck at the 'upgrade' menu for entire minutes with a frozen and non responsive UI, unable even to close it and re open
In ALL play - you will have stuttering at seemingly random intervals from every 4 seconds to sometimes if very lucky, 40 to 50 seconds between.

Dodge a boss attack? Stutter! and get hit anyway ..
Mob spawn nearby? Stutter! ..
Dodge an Elite mob? Stutter! and dodge is now on cooldown and did not function ...
or Dodge an Elite mob? sure! but you got hit anyway .. the melee attacks do not use actual 'real time' collisions but seem to be scripted events on the player actor - the melee units can even be facing the other way .. and you will be staggered / interupted
Hit your Ultimate? Stutter! and now it is on cooldown and did not go off ...

And, as is usual with scammy Gacha games, the "developers" have not shown or voiced ANY intention of addressing these issues. The game has had some maintenance with 0 improvement in this regard - some reports of it being worse.

If performance issues being the main challenge of the game play is not a problem, then this game is actually quite fun.

If value is to be "you get what you pay for" and the Free to play used as an excuse .. this game is actually way too expensive (even as free)

Edit 12 Aug 2025 - there has been an update to address many issues with the game and bug "fixes" 
This maintenance has seemed to make every issue considerably worse. The stuttering is even more inconvenient than it was - in fact almost all of the game's functions are worse.

Edit 20 Aug 2025 - Stuttering is worse, Overall performance is worse. Every successive "update" downgrades performance.
The stuttering was inconvenient at first, and now after some fixes it is unplayable. The UI is so laggy it too is almost unuseable at times (as annoyingly inconsistent as the stuttering issues)  I finally gave up and just uninstalled ...

I usually leave good reviews but this was genuinely horrible. 
I'd like to start by saying that just because I came from discord does not mean I automatically was going to leave a bad review, I played it because it looked genuinely fun.
upon release the game had ONE free character and a second after playing for three days... They did fix this and release a couple more for free upon completion of the first mission, however there still are characters behind paywalls, there is a battle pass, characters for sale, and a gacha system. This game has more in-app purchases than Genshin and worse fighting. 
On the topic of fighting: If you dash to the side out of the impact zone of an attack, you expect to dodge the attack, right? wrong. When I was in a boss fight the boss leaped into the air so I dashed out of the way, the boss then REDIRECTED mid air to land ontop of me dealing damage. An argument could be made that you need to dodge later, I have dashed when the rectangle appeared, after it was on me for a second, and right when it was about to hit me. There is a tiny window right before the attack hits that you can dodge in.
Boss fights feel very long and repetitive. I played through a few missions and encountered a total of 3 bosses. Big guy, sword guy, and worm. 
Big guy jumps on you, sword guy swings at you, worm charges at you. The snake or worm boss has a few unique mechanics like hiding behind a wall and launching orbs at you but there are so many rounds to it. There are "phases" but the attacks are the same for all the phases and the only change is the last phase where the worm leaves the original point it was stuck at, yes. the boss is stuck in one point for about 2/3rds of the fight. 

Overall: gameplay is repetitive, everything is paywalled. You'd be better off playing a scummy mobile game because it probably would have less pay walls.

This is another situation where I really wish steam had a mixed review option. I don’t really recommend Four or against this game. If you are really bored and are in need of a very basic third person shooter action rogue like game to burn some time while you watch YouTube on a second monitor then this game fits the bill. It doesn’t do anything to innovate or push forward the genre. I can’t find anything about it. That would make me recommend you play this instead of the numerous incredible action rogue like that exist. But there is also nothing about it. That makes me recommend you don’t play it. It’s just completely fine in every respect. The character designs are fine. The art style is fine. The shooting is fine. The bosses are fine. As far as monetization, I can’t really comment because I have barely looked at the shop due to the fact that nothing about this game motivates me to even consider spending money on it. It’s free try it for yourself and see if you like it. Maybe you’ll get a few hours of enjoyment while you wait for your next game that you’re excited about to release. The only strong emotion that this game gives me is a little bit of disappointment that so many games like this get made and shut down within a year. They push out the most bare bones version of some popular genre as free to play and stuff it full of micro transactions in the hopes to make some QuickBooks and then as soon as the player drops off, they kill it. They are a dime, a dozen on mobile storefronts and steam. Most of them have some sort of anime or cartoon or fantasy aesthetic. Anyway, I just wish the people talented enough to make and ship games spend their time making something actually creative and exciting and that they wanted to make. But so long as games like Genshin continue to rake in billions of dollars we will keep getting games like this that launch with a couple thousand players and then die within a year and all of the time and effort and art that went into making them is erased forever.

The game is pretty fun. A roguelike you play with friends. The bosses are fun and so far, I haven't had issues with the game play. The problem I have is with the Matchmaking System. It exists, but that is a stretch. You can sit in queue to find a group for a very long time or it can let you jump in solo. In a group, the "match" is 20 minutes, Solo, it took me an hour. I completed it, but there was no way in hell I was going to get the next difficulty unlock since I had to beat it in 29 minutes....

I mentioned Matchmaking in the in game chat and people said get some friends to play. If a creator is only relying on groups to play together, then why have matchmaking? Make it easier for solo queue or actually fix the system. 

I reiterate, Matchmaking will be the death of this game and it is a shame.

While I can see why people dislike the game and I do have some problems with the amount of microtransactions. I still love the gameplay so far and I see a promising future for the game if the devs listen to the feedback of the playerbase.

So far so good, enjoying the game.  
- THANK YOU for letting us do levels solo if we want.  I've been in queue sometimes for a while with no one to join. 
- I like the progression of power while playing.  
- Seems like most of the pay items are cosmetic, which makes me want to keep playing.
- Character models are clean, though some seem like a direct ripoff of Overwatch.

My only grip is the lag every so often during fights.  Though not game breaking, it is annoying when being precise in your game play.  This occurs solo or in a party.

Reminds me greatly of some old games I miss that are now unplayable.

The aesthetic is awesome, the small list of characters is varied, the levels are somewhat repetitive but that's a compliment from me - I enjoy simple game-play loops that don't boggle my brain. 

I did have some rather major lag issues on first launch, but on my second run they seemed to be almost gone so I can't complain.

As an overly antisocial little hermit crab, this is totally fine in single-player too if you keep to the low difficulties as a noob like me and it's nicely refreshing from the constant flood of PvP games I've played, disliked or even obsessed over for years.

Very fun game, although new, it has little bugs as far as I've seen so far, though of course it also means the amount of content is somewhat lacking, but I'm sure that will be changed in future updates. I haven't experienced any of the stuttering mentioned in other reviews, and I'm running almost the bare minimum specs (I'm brokie). The characters control well, combat feels fun though gets repetitive fairly quickly, and there's a quite limited pool of upgrades. I'm looking forward to this game's future.

While fighting a mechanical snake boss I was holding left mouse, dodging, and pressing abilities just thinking "what the hell am i doing in this game right now?"
This game feels like it has no soul. Some slop games try to keep players engaged just enough to enter their credit card info, but this game doesn't even do that well. 
Also, the stuttering is really bad. 2-5 second stutter every 10 or so seconds on a 12th gen i7, 3080, with 32 ram.
The gameplay has potential but the artstyle looks like trash chinese p2w game. I would recommend the game if they improve upon it.
